title: DNS picks the region and the balancer picks the VM
summary: A store sells to Mexico and Spain under a single domain, tienda.mx, from northamerica-south1 and europe-southwest1. If a region fails, shoppers must reach the other one within minutes.

requirements.1: {{s1}} publishes a single name, tienda.mx, and answers with the address of the healthy region closest to the shopper, with a 60 s TTL.
requirements.2: {{s2}} probes from several points on the internet, at a set interval, that each region's balancer answers; if one fails, slot 1 stops announcing it.
requirements.3: {{s3}} receives HTTPS in region A, terminates TLS and spreads requests only across the web VMs that pass their health check.
requirements.4: {{s4}} keeps at least 2 web VMs in region A in different zones, replaces the one that fails and adds more when the load goes up.
requirements.5: {{s5}} delivers the alarm's alert to the on-call team when slot 2 marks a region as down; the repair clock starts with that alert.
requirements.6: {{s6}} does in region B what slot 3 does in A: terminates TLS and spreads requests only across the healthy web VMs.
requirements.7: {{s7}} does what slot 4 does, for the web VMs in region B: at least 2 in different zones, replaces the one that fails and adds more with the load.

s1.explanation: Cloud DNS routing policies in a public zone can be geolocation (the nearest match to where the query comes from) or failover, and they only return healthy addresses.
s1.hint_cue: answers with the address of the healthy region closest

s2.explanation: For external endpoints you create a health check that probes from three Google Cloud regions, for example over HTTPS, every 30 to 300 s; it only works in public zones, and the policy only returns healthy addresses.
s2.hint_cue: probes from several points on the internet

s3.explanation: The regional external Application Load Balancer is an Envoy proxy that terminates TLS in a single region with its target HTTPS proxy, and its backend service only sends requests to healthy backends.

s4.explanation: A managed instance group recreates the VMs its autohealing health check finds unhealthy, and the autoscaler adds VMs when the load goes up. An unmanaged group cannot use the autoscaler.
s4.hint_cue: replaces the one that fails and adds more

s5.explanation: Cloud Monitoring notification channels alert the on-call team when an alerting policy fires, by email, SMS, Slack, PagerDuty or the console mobile app.
s5.hint_cue: delivers the alarm's alert to the on-call team

s6.explanation: In region B another regional external Application Load Balancer terminates TLS in that region, and its backend service only sends requests to healthy backends.
s6.hint_cue: terminates TLS and spreads requests only across the healthy web VMs

s7.explanation: Region B has its own managed instance group: it recreates the VMs its autohealing health check finds unhealthy, and the autoscaler adds VMs when the load goes up.
s7.hint_cue: replaces the one that fails and adds more with the load

gcp-dns-server-policy.s1: Server policies apply private DNS settings to a VPC network, such as forwarding and logging, for hybrid resolution; they do not publish tienda.mx or pick the healthy region.

gcp-backend-health-check.s2: The backend service health check watches the balancer's backends so only the healthy ones get requests; in a public zone, the DNS policy uses external endpoint health checks instead, which probe from three Google Cloud regions.

gcp-api-gateway.s3: API Gateway is for creating, sharing, maintaining and securing REST APIs; this slot needs a regional proxy that terminates TLS and spreads requests across Compute Engine instance groups by their health check.
gcp-api-gateway.s6: API Gateway is for creating, sharing, maintaining and securing REST APIs; this slot needs a regional proxy that terminates TLS and spreads requests across Compute Engine instance groups by their health check.

gcp-unmanaged-ig.s4: An unmanaged instance group groups VMs, but only managed groups can use the autoscaler to add VMs with the load.
gcp-unmanaged-ig.s7: An unmanaged instance group groups VMs, but only managed groups can use the autoscaler to add VMs with the load.

gcp-compute-engine.s4: Each web VM in the diagram is already a Compute Engine VM; the slot asks for what recreates unhealthy VMs and adds more when the load goes up.
gcp-compute-engine.s7: Each web VM in the diagram is already a Compute Engine VM; the slot asks for what recreates unhealthy VMs and adds more when the load goes up.

gcp-cloud-logging.s5: Cloud Logging is the system that stores, searches and analyzes logs; the slot asks for the piece through which Cloud Monitoring alerts the on-call team when an alerting policy fires.
